opportunities.title: 974 and Counting: Inside the Biggest Patch Tuesday in History (and Why Your Backlog Just Got Worse)
opportunities.why_now: Microsoft just shattered its own CVE record with 974 fixes in a single Patch Tuesday, including two zero-days already under active exploitation.
opportunities.angle: Data-driven breakdown of the 974 CVEs by severity/product, with a triage cheat-sheet for sysadmins on what to patch first (the two exploited zero-days) vs. what can wait

opportunities.title: SAP's CVSS 10.0 Kernel Bug: The Perfect Unauthenticated RCE Nobody's Talking About Enough
opportunities.why_now: A maximum-severity, pre-auth remote code execution flaw in SAP's kernel is exactly the kind of thing ransomware crews build automated exploit chains around within days.
opportunities.angle: Explainer on why CVSS 10.0 + unauthenticated + kernel-level is a worst-case combo, with a countdown framing (days until mass exploitation) and patch-now call to action

opportunities.title: F5's Invisible Web Shell: Malware That Lives in Memory So Your AV Never Sees It
opportunities.why_now: F5 BIG-IP APM malware injecting PHP web shells directly into memory to dodge disk scans is a fresh evasion technique enterprise defenders need to know about now.
opportunities.angle: Technical deep-dive on the memory-resident evasion technique, what detection signatures actually catch it, and why disk-based AV is increasingly obsolete

opportunities.title: Chrome's Seventh Zero-Day of 2026: The V8 Sandbox Escape Nobody Can Ignore
opportunities.why_now: Chrome 153 just patched an actively-exploited V8 zero-day enabling code execution inside the sandbox — the seventh this year, a pace worth flagging.
opportunities.angle: Trend piece tracking Chrome's 2026 zero-day count as a barometer for browser exploit markets, urging immediate update with a simple 'check your Chrome version' CTA

opportunities.title: AI Agents Now Hack Faster Than You Can Read This Sentence: 6 Hours, Thousands of Credentials
opportunities.why_now: A fresh report shows autonomous AI agents compromising thousands of credentials in under six hours — a concrete, alarming benchmark for AI-driven attack speed.
opportunities.angle: Feature framing this as the arrival of 'AI-speed breaches,' contrasting traditional incident response timelines against six-hour agent-driven compromise, ending on what defenders can realistically do
